note: Both texts are faithful; the differences are minor (X 'utiliſsimus' where the leaf prints 'vtiliſsimus'; Y puts the catchword 'terminum' in meta instead of the text).
X drops 殺 in '摠殺漢官' (losing 'killed the Han officials'), drops 主 in '主簿' and drops 平 in '向府平論', all of which the leaf prints.
The leaf reads 'disputatione abijciatur' and 'quenquam', which Y has; X gives 'disputione abjiciatur' and 'quemquam'.
The title word is 'SENTENTIAE', but X reads it as 'TENTIAB'; Y also records the struck-through inscription and the motto 'VIRTVTE DVCE, COMITE FORTVNA'.
In letter XLII X leaves out 'ob' in 'si ob intermissionem obsequia', which the leaf prints; otherwise the two are identical.
The leaf reads 'statutis sublatis sua substituerunt'; X has 'oblatis' and drops 'sua', and also gives 'quod diceros' where Y has 'quasi diceres'.
The entry for page 429 is 'De iureiurando', but X gives a wrong heading, 'De inveniendo'.

Where the passage is obscured by show-through, X misreads it as 'veterum gentium ritibus & caeremoniis, ad philosophandi rationem' and 'probatur', while Y matches the leaf: 'cæterarum gentium ritibus, cæremonijs, ac philosophandi ratione' and 'probaturi'.
Y has many wrong words that change the sense ('pulsa' for 'pusca', 'puniceū' for 'feniceū', 'agris' for 'areis', 'De ōes' for '⁊ oēs'), and its side-letters A/B/D/F do not match the printed G–N.
Y misreads long s as 'f' throughout and drops whole phrases ('Magis exigas. Magis uitae longitudinem' and 'deus uoluntatem pro effectu coronabit ... quid utili-').
